interventions.name: Light surfaces
interventions.summary: The NYSERDA comparative source ranks light surfaces among the cheapest cooling options per degree of temperature reduction.
interventions.sourceNote: Real ranking evidence only. This repository still does not claim a city-specific unit price from this source.

interventions.name: Cool roofs
interventions.summary: The NYSERDA comparative source places light roofs among the cheaper heat-island mitigation options per degree of cooling.
interventions.sourceNote: Priority ordering is source-backed, but no Boston-ready unit cost is claimed here.

interventions.name: Curbside planting
interventions.summary: The NYSERDA comparative source indicates curbside planting is more cost-effective per degree of cooling than street trees.
interventions.sourceNote: Real comparative evidence only. No per-tree procurement price is asserted from this source.

interventions.name: Street trees
interventions.summary: The NYSERDA comparative source says street trees are less cost-effective per degree of cooling than light surfaces, light roofs, and curbside planting.
interventions.sourceNote: This is a real ranking result, not a city-specific planting cost table.

interventions.name: Cool pavement
interventions.summary: Cool pavement can lower surface temperatures on selected streets and plazas, but the catalog still needs a verified seed row before the app treats it as a costed procurement item.
interventions.sourceNote: Public reporting citing ASCE describes a cool-pavement sealant premium of about $0.60 per square yard. The matching verified unit-cost seed row lives in the separate unit-cost file.

interventions.name: Shade structures
interventions.summary: Public shade structures can quickly cool hard-play or plaza spaces, but the catalog still needs a verified unit-cost row before the app treats them as costed procurement items.
interventions.sourceNote: Public reporting notes that some playground shade structures can cost upward of $95,000; this entry remains ranking-only until a procurement source is added.

interventions.name: Green roofs
interventions.summary: Green roofs are a related cooling action that can be costed from public case-study examples, but this repo still needs a verified row before treating them as procurement-ready.
interventions.sourceNote: Public case-study examples in the literature show extensive green roofs can be costed from real project totals; the repo still needs the matching verified unit-cost row.

interventions.name: Green walls
interventions.summary: Green walls can cool building edges and adjacent sidewalks through shading and evapotranspiration, especially where horizontal tree canopy is hard to add.
interventions.sourceNote: Review coverage of GCCAR findings notes that green walls significantly mitigate surrounding heat and are useful where ground-space tree planting is constrained.

interventions.name: Permeable paving
interventions.summary: Permeable paving supports evaporative cooling, reduces runoff, and can improve near-surface comfort in heat-exposed plazas and low-traffic streets.
interventions.sourceNote: The literature describes heat-island mitigation benefits from reflective and permeable paving and its compatibility with stormwater control.

interventions.name: Pocket parks
interventions.summary: Pocket parks convert very small leftover sites into human-scale cooling spaces with seating, shade, and vegetation.
interventions.sourceNote: Pocket parks are a related micro-space intervention that can be paired with shade and planting; this entry becomes verified only when a seed cost row is present.

interventions.name: Transit shade canopies
interventions.summary: Shade canopies at transit stops and other waiting areas cut direct solar exposure where people are forced to stand still in the heat.
interventions.sourceNote: Shaded routing research shows that localized shade along mobility corridors produces disproportionate heat-exposure benefits, supporting transit-stop shade as a targeted intervention.

interventions.name: Whole-city cooling package
interventions.summary: A literature-cited Los Angeles package provides a coarse whole-city benchmark of about US$1B for large-scale cooling action.
interventions.sourceNote: Use this only as a macro benchmark for exhaustive planning, not as a substitute for per-action unit costs.
